subject.title: [Bug]: Codex quota recovery/reset credits do not re-probe long WHAM cooldowns when fallbacks exist

question: Should a WHAM `subscription_limit` reset remain authoritative while a fallback is healthy, or should OpenClaw periodically half-open and retry the blocked model before that reset?
rationale: Current code and docs intentionally avoid early probes for recorded provider reset windows, while earlier probing trades faster recovery against extra quota usage, latency, and repeated hard-limit requests.

options.title: Add bounded model-scoped probes
options.body: Periodically retry only the blocked model/profile and re-arm the recorded block when the upstream still returns a subscription-limit response.

options.title: Keep reset authoritative
options.body: Retain the current behavior and document that early account or sibling-model recovery does not invalidate the blocked model's reset deadline.

options.title: Require same-model proof first
options.body: Wait for the model-scoping work and a live post-block `gpt-5.5` success before selecting a permanent probe policy.

recommendation.title: Add bounded model-scoped probes
recommendation.body: Periodically retry only the blocked model/profile and re-arm the recorded block when the upstream still returns a subscription-limit response.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent fallback and agent-scope history makes this the strongest available routing candidate for the cross-path policy choice.
